BRIGHT DAY — a clear blue sky arches over the village, warm sunlight dappling through the canopy, golden motes drifting lazily between mossy rooftops and flower-draped doorways.
GOLDEN HOUR — the sun hangs low and honey-warm, flooding the village in long amber light, every surface gilded, glowing motes drifting slow and bright between the eaves.
SUNSET — a blazing sky of pink and burnt-orange and gold spreads above the treetops, warm rim-light glowing on every rooftop, the first amber windows just beginning to shine.
PURPLE TWILIGHT — a violet-and-indigo dusk deepens over the rooftops, warm golden lanterns flickering on along the paths, glowing windows reflecting softly in the dewy moss below.
LANTERN-LIT NIGHT — a deep indigo sky thick with stars, the whole village aglow with swaying lanterns and warm windows, fireflies weaving between bioluminescent mushrooms shining in the dark.
FIRST MORNING LIGHT — pale pink dawn seeps through a thin mist, the village hushed and soft, a few lanterns still burning gold, dewy rooftops catching the first blush of light.
RAINY — soft grey rain falls steadily, every rooftop and cobblestone wet and gleaming, cozy amber windows glowing warmly through the misty drizzle, eaves dripping, the whole village hushed and snug.
